statement: Micron projects $22 billion of cash deposits and related financial commitments under signed take-or-pay memory supply agreements
why: Customers prepaying billions of dollars to lock in memory supply is a hard commitment signal that AI accelerator demand is being pulled forward through the memory chain.

impact.mechanism: Prepaid take-or-pay deposits convert expected AI accelerator build-out into contracted memory revenue and fund the memory capacity that gates accelerator module output.

evidence.excerpt: Under the SEAs we have signed so far, we project to receive cash deposits and related financial commitments of $22 billion.
roughly $18 billion of that is cash deposits, with the balance in letters of credit.

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet restating figures first disclosed on Micron's fiscal Q3 FY2026 earnings call; no primary filing or transcript fetched, and the two named corroborating pieces were not independently fetched.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: value 100.0 -> 22.0 (tol 1%); sources: 24/7 Wall St.
